_provenance.primary_source: NOAA Pacific Marine Environmental Laboratory (PMEL) & Alaska Ocean Acidification Network
secondary_sources: Mathis, J.T. et al. (2015). Ocean acidification risk assessment for Alaska's fishery sector. Progress in Oceanography 136:71-91.
Long, W.C. et al. (2013). Effects of ocean acidification on juvenile red king crab and Tanner crab. PLoS ONE 8(4).
_provenance.notes: Alaska seas are experiencing ocean acidification (OA) faster than any other open-ocean region on Earth due to cold water absorbing more atmospheric CO2 and seasonal upwelling. NOAA PMEL monitoring shows aragonite undersaturation (Ω aragonite < 1.0) occurring during winter in the Bering Sea and Gulf of Alaska. Laboratory studies confirm that OA reduces juvenile Red King Crab and Tanner Crab shell calcification and survival by 30-70%, posing long-term risks to shellfish and pteropod-based forage food webs.

species_vulnerability_matrix.impact: High — Reduced larval survival & calcification in Ω < 1.0 waters
High — Decreased carapace hardness and 50% higher mortality rate
Critical — Shell dissolution occurring in 20% of GOA surface samples
Moderate — Indirect impact via pteropod prey loss in North Pacific
Low — Direct physiological impact mild, prey shift resilience high
